title: Bombshell Endorsement Shakes Michigan Senate Race as Democrat Haley Stevens Backs GOP's Mike Rogers
snippet: Just days before Election Day, Representative Haley Stevens delivered a shocking endorsement for Republican Mike Rogers, injecting intense uncertainty into Michigan's razor-thin Senate race against progressive Abdul El-Sayed.
content:
In a stunning final-hour twist in one of the nation's most fiercely contested Senate battles, Democratic Representative Haley Stevens has broken ranks to endorse Republican nominee Mike Rogers in Michigan's marquee midterm race.

The shock endorsement came just two days before voters head to the polls to decide who will succeed retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters. Stevens, who narrowly lost a heated Democratic primary to progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed in August, publicly threw her support behind Rogers after the two attended service together at Detroit's Perfecting Church on Sunday.

A Fractured Party and a Public Fallout

"Our Democratic nominee for Senate said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away," Stevens revealed in a video announcement. "And he's right. And that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today."

The unprecedented intraparty break followed escalating tensions over campaign messaging regarding Israel and foreign policy. Tensions boiled over when Stevens demanded El-Sayed denounce a controversial third-party ad linking U.S. support for Israel to rising domestic grocery prices. When El-Sayed's team asked Stevens to step back from joint campaign appearances, the Democratic congresswoman made the decision to switch allegiances, sparking staff resignations in her own office and chaos within state party lines.

High Stakes in the Great Lakes State

The Michigan contest carries monumental stakes for Capitol Hill, as control of the U.S. Senate hangs in the balance. El-Sayed, a 42-year-old physician, Rhodes Scholar, and former Detroit health director, is attempting to become the nation's first Muslim senator on an unapologetically progressive platform featuring Medicare for All and an end to U.S. military aid to Israel.

Rogers, 63, a former FBI agent and House Intelligence Committee chairman, offers a stark contrast as a national security conservative. Running in a swing state that went for Donald Trump in 2024, Rogers has targeted Black and Jewish voters in suburban and urban centers—constituencies that heavily favored Stevens during the August primary.

Uncertainty at the Polls

Prior to Stevens' surprise announcement, October surveys showed El-Sayed holding a narrow lead ranging from 1 to 7 percentage points. However, political analysts note that none of the public polling reflects the potential fallout from Stevens' high-profile crossover.

With Michigan cementing its reputation as a battleground state decided by slim margins, Tuesday's vote will measure whether El-Sayed's progressive base can carry him over the finish line—or if Rogers can capitalize on Democratic division to deliver Republicans a vital Senate flip.
